description: Demolition of existing site buildings (excluding the retained central timber-framed barn), removal of existing hardstanding including the menage, change of use of part of the land to a workshop use (Use Class E(g)(iii)), and redevelopment of previously developed land to provide a workshop building with associated parking, hard and soft landscaping, formation of a pond, regrading of land levels, improvements to the existing access, sustainable drainage measures, and on-site biodiversity net gain enhancements.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
REASON
To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Notwithstanding the red line application boundary, the change of use to Use Class E(g)(iii) hereby permitted shall be limited solely to the area identified as the "Workshop Precinct Area" on Drawing No. 1469-0032 Site Zoning Map. The areas identified as the "Landscape Works Area" and "Spoil Relocation Area" shall remain in their existing lawful use and shall not be used for any purpose ancillary to the workshop use, including the storage of materials, vehicles, machinery, equipment or finished products, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
REASON

To ensure that the extent of the approved change of use is appropriately limited, to safeguard the openness of the Green Belt and the rural character of the area, and to prevent the encroachment of commercial activities into surrounding land, in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies G2, D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMHB 1 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local P

Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved plans and supporting documents, no above-ground works shall commence until details and samples of all external facing materials to be used in the construction of the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include, but not be limited to, the proposed masonry, metal cladding, roofing materials, glazing, external doors, windows and rainwater goods. The development shall thereafter be carried out in strict accordance with the approved details and retained as such thereafter.
REASON

To ensure that the development achieves a high standard of design and appearance, preserves the rural character of the site and its surroundings, and safeguards the significance and setting of the retained non-designated heritage asset, in accordance with Policy DP3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies D4 and HC1 of the London Plan (2021), Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Lo

Prior to the commencement of above-ground works, detailed drawings at an appropriate scale (minimum 1:20 and 1:5 where appropriate) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority showing the architectural detailing of the development, including windows, doors, reveals, eaves, verges, rainwater goods, glazed links, and the junctions between the proposed metal cladding and masonry, together with details of their fixing and finish. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
REASON

To ensure a high quality of design and detailing which preserves the character of the area and the significance of the retained heritage asset, in accordance with Policy D4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).
Prior to the commencement of above-ground works, a landscape scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include:
(i) Details of all existing and proposed hard landscaping, including finished levels or contours;

(ii) Details of all proposed soft landscaping, including planting plans, written specifications (including cultivation and other operations associated with plant and grass establishment), schedules of plants noting species, plant sizes and proposed numbers/densities;
(iii) Details of boundary treatments;

(iv) Details of the hard and soft landscaping within the arrival space surrounding the retained timber-framed barn, including paving materials, planting, street furniture (where proposed), and the relationship with the adjacent vehicle parking areas, to ensure that the setting of the retained heritage asset is of a high quality and not dominated by parking; and
(v) A programme for implementation and long-term managemen

Prior to the commencement of above-ground works, a replacement tree planting scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include details of the number, species, size, location and specification of all replacement trees and shall demonstrate that the loss of trees associated with the development is appropriately compensated through replacement planting elsewhere within the site. The approved planting shall be carried out in the first planting season following completion of the development or first occupation, whichever is sooner, and any trees which die, are removed or become seriously damaged or diseased within five years of planting shall be replaced in the next planting season with others of similar size and species.
REASON

To ensure that the loss of existing trees is appropriately mitigated and that the development contributes positively to the landscape character, visual amenity and biodiversity of the site, in accordance

The development shall be carried out in full accordance with the approved Arboricultural Impact Assessment, Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan contained within the Arboricultural Report dated 2nd February 2026 by Crown Tree Consultancy. All tree protection measures, protective fencing and ground protection shall be installed before any demolition, site clearance or construction works commence (excluding those required to install the protection measures) and shall be retained for the duration of the works. No excavation, level changes, storage of materials, parking of vehicles, mixing of cement, fires or other operations likely to damage retained trees shall take place within the protected areas unless expressly provided for in the approved documents.
REASON

To ensure the protection and long-term retention of trees to be retained on the site, in accordance with Policies G5 and G7 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies DMHB 11 and DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Pl

Prior to the installation of any underground services within the Root Protection Areas of retained trees, details of the routing and installation methodology shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submitted details shall demonstrate how impacts on retained trees and their root systems will be avoided or minimised, having regard to the recommendations of BS 5837:2012. The works shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
REASON

To safeguard the health and longevity of retained trees and their Root Protection Areas during construction, in accordance with Policies G5 and G7 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies DMHB 11 and DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

No development (excluding demolition and site clearance) shall commence until a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The CLP shall include details of:
- The phasing and programme of construction works
- Construction vehicle routing to and from the site
- Arrangements for the delivery and storage of plant, equipment and materials
- Contractor parking and welfare facilities
- Loading, unloading and turning arrangements within the site
- Measures to prevent mud and debris being deposited on the public highway, including wheel washing facilities where appropriate
- Arrangements for managing construction traffic so as to minimise disruption to the local highway network
- Measures to protect pedestrian and highway safety
- The name and contact details of the site manager and procedures for dealing with complaints.
The development shall thereafter be carried out strictly in accordance with the approved Construction

(i) The development hereby permitted (excluding demolition, site clearance and initial ground investigation works) shall not commence until a scheme to deal with unacceptable contamination, (including asbestos materials detected within the soil), has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority (LPA). All works which form part of any required remediation scheme shall be completed before any part of the development is occupied or brought into use unless the Local Planning Authority dispenses with any such requirement specifically and in writing. The scheme shall include the following measures unless the LPA dispenses with any such requirement specifically and in writing:

(a) A site investigation, including where relevant soil, soil gas, surface water, and groundwater sampling, together with the results of analysis and risk assessment shall be carried out by a suitably qualified and accredited consultant/contractor. The report should also clearly identify all risks, li

Prior to commencement (except for demolition, ground and enabling work) any relevant phase of this development (excluding demolition and site clearance), a scheme for the provision of sustainable water management shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with the relevant stakeholders. The scheme shall clearly demonstrate how it manages water and demonstrate ways of controlling the surface water on site by providing information on:
a) Sustainable Drainage features:

i. Surface water discharge - the submitted drainage strategy must identify the proposed method and location of discharging collected surface water from the site in accordance with the hierarchy set out in Policy SI 13 of the London Plan (2021). Where the proposal does not utilise the most sustainable solution, justification must be provided.
ii. SuDS - the submitted drainage strategy should incorporate Sustainable Drainage System (SuDS) elements that are embedded, where

No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
REASON

To comply with the National Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems, Policy F8 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), the London Plan (Policies SI 12 and SI 13) along with associated guidance to these policies and Policy EM6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012).
The development hereby approved shall not be commenced unless:
(a) A Biodiversity Gain Plan has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority; and
(b) The Local Planning Authority has approved the plan.
REASON

To ensure the development delivers biodiversity net gain in accordance with Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Policy N2 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

Prior to the commencement of development (excluding demolition, site clearance and approved ecological survey works), an Ecological Mitigation and Enhancement Plan (EMEP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include:
a) measures for the protection of protected and notable species during construction, including reptiles, hedgehogs, nesting birds, badgers and hazel dormice;
b) details of ecological supervision and the role of any Ecological Clerk of Works;
c) details of ecological enhancement measures, including the number, specification and location of bird boxes, bat boxes and other wildlife features;
d) details of native planting and habitat enhancement measures not otherwise secured through the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;
e) measures for the treatment and management of invasive non-native species; and
f) a timetable for implementation.
The approved measures shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and

Prior to above-ground works, details of bat compensation and enhancement measures shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the number, specification, location and timing of installation of bat boxes, bat bricks, bat tiles and any other bat roosting features. The approved measures shall be installed prior to first occupation of the development and thereafter retained.
REASON

To compensate for the loss of bat roosting habitat and enhance biodiversity in accordance with Policy N2 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026) and Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

No development (excluding demolition, site clearance and ecological survey works) shall commence until a Great Crested Newt Mitigation Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
The Strategy shall be informed by updated surveys of the ponds within 250m of the site and shall include:
(i) details of any required European Protected Species Mitigation Licence;
(ii) details of exclusion fencing, trapping and translocation measures;
(iii) details of habitat retention, creation and enhancement measures;
(iv) details of ecological supervision during construction;
(v) a timetable for implementation; and
(vi) details of post-development monitoring where required.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Strategy.
REASON
To ensure the protection of great crested newts and their habitats and to ensure compliance with the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended), the Conservation of Habitats and Species Re
The external lighting hereby approved shall be installed and operated in accordance with the approved Lighting Strategy Plan (Drawing No. P_00_003 Rev P05) and shall thereafter be retained as such.

No additional external lighting shall be installed on the site, including along the access driveway, within the parkland areas, or along the pedestrian route linking the workshop to the shooting grounds, unless details have first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
All external lighting shall be directed downwards and shielded to minimise light spill beyond the application site and shall be operated only in accordance with the approved details.
REASON

To safeguard the rural character of the area, minimise light pollution, protect biodiversity and neighbouring amenity, in accordance with Policy P3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy DMEI 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policy G6 of the London Plan (2021).

A) No development shall take place until the applicant has secured the implementation of a programme of archaeological works in accordance with a Written Scheme of Investigation which has been submitted by the applicant and approved by the local planning authority.
B) No development or demolition shall take place other that in accordance with the Written Scheme of Investigation approved under Part (A).

C) The development shall not be occupied until the site investigation and post investigation assessment has been completed in accordance with the programme set out in the Written Scheme of Investigation approved under Part (A), and the provision made for analysis, publication and dissemination of the results and archive deposition has been secured.
REASON

To ensure that archaeological remains of interest on the site are appropriately investigated, recorded, analysed and archived prior to and during development, in accordance with Policies HE5 and HE10 of the National Planning Policy
No demolition of the buildings identified for removal shall commence until a programme of historic building recording has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The programme of recording shall be undertaken by a suitably qualified heritage professional and shall include a written scheme of investigation setting out the scope, methodology and timetable for the recording works. The level of recording shall be proportionate to the significance of the buildings and shall include a photographic survey, measured drawings where appropriate, and a written record of the buildings' form, fabric, construction and historic development.

The approved recording shall be completed prior to demolition and a copy of the final report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The report shall also be deposited with the Greater London Historic Environment Record and any other relevant local archive as appropriate.
REASON
To ensure

Prior to the commencement of any alteration, repair or conversion works to the retained timber-framed barn, and following the removal of all contents other than its fixtures, fittings and built fabric, all works to the barn shall cease until access has been provided to the Historic England Scientific Team and/or their appointed contractors to undertake dendrochronological sampling and analysis of the structure.
The sampling shall be carried out in conjunction with a suitably qualified bat ecologist to ensure that the works do not adversely affect any protected species or their roosts.

A copy of the final dendrochronological report shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in PDF format within 12 months of the sampling being undertaken. Where dendrochronological dating is demonstrated to be scientifically unfeasible, written confirmation and justification shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority as soon as reasonably practicable following completion of the assessmen

The development shall not be occupied until the refuse and recycling storage facilities shown on the approved plans have been provided and made available for use. The facilities shall thereafter be retained for the storage of refuse and recycling and shall not be used for any other purpose.
REASON

To ensure the provision of satisfactory facilities for the storage and collection of waste and recycling in the interests of visual amenity and the proper operation of the development, in accordance with Policy DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

Prior to first occupation of the development, a minimum of one active Electric Vehicle Charging Point and one passive Electric Vehicle Charging Point shall be provided within the approved parking area. The charging infrastructure shall thereafter be retained, maintained and kept available for use for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To encourage the uptake of electric vehicles and reduce emissions from road transport in accordance with Policy T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

The development shall not be occupied until the vehicle parking spaces, disabled parking spaces, vehicle turning areas, cycle parking facilities, motorcycle parking facilities and electric vehicle charging infrastructure shown on the approved plans have been provided and made available for use.
The approved facilities shall thereafter be retained solely for their designated purposes and shall not be used for any other purpose.
REASON

To ensure adequate off-street parking, turning and sustainable transport facilities are provided in the interests of highway safety and sustainable transport, in accordance with Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policies T4, T5 and T6 of the London Plan (2021).

The development shall not be occupied until the access improvements shown on Drawing No. 3024001/SK/1A (or equivalent approved drawing), including the widened site access, passing place and associated junction improvements with Ducks Hill Road, have been completed in accordance with the approved details.
REASON

To ensure safe and convenient access to the site in the interests of highway and pedestrian safety, in accordance with Policies DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021).
Prior to first occupation of the development, a Workplace Travel Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Travel Plan shall include:
- Measures to encourage sustainable travel by staff and visitors, including walking, cycling, public transport and car sharing
- Details of the appointment of a Travel Plan Co-ordinator
- Targets for reducing single-occupancy vehicle trips
- A programme for implementation, monitoring and review
- Mechanisms for periodic reporting to the Local Planning Authority.
The approved Travel Plan shall thereafter be implemented, monitored and maintained in accordance with its approved details for the lifetime of the development.
REASON

To promote sustainable travel choices, reduce reliance on the private car and mitigate the transport impacts of the development, in accordance with Policies TR3, TR4 and TR6 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMT 1 and DM
The workshop hereby approved shall not be used except between the following hours:
07:00 to 23:00 Mondays to Fridays;
07:00 to 23:00 Saturdays;
07:00 to 23:00 Sundays and Bank Holidays.
The operation of fixed plant and machinery associated with the development may continue outside these hours in accordance with the approved Noise Impact Assessment.
REASON

To safeguard the amenities of nearby occupiers and the rural character of the area, in accordance with Policies DMHB 11 and EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020), Policies D3 and D14 of the London Plan (2021), and the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The workshop building hereby approved shall be used only for purposes falling within Use Class E(g)(iii) of the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), and for no other purpose, including any other use within Class E, or any equivalent provision in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification. For the avoidance of doubt, Use Class E(g)(iii) refers to 'any industrial process, being a use, which can be carried out in any residential area without detriment to the amenity of that area by reason of noise, vibration, smell, fumes, smoke, soot, ash, dust or grit.'
REASON

To ensure that the use of the site remains compatible with the rural character of the area, the Green Belt, the retained heritage assets and nearby ecological interests, and to prevent the establishment of alternative uses that could give rise to materially different impacts on residential or visual amenity, in accordance with Policies DMT 1, DMT 2, DMEI 7

No materials, machinery, equipment, waste, skips, containers, finished products or other items associated with the use of the site shall be stored outside the buildings hereby approved, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans or first agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
REASON

To safeguard the openness of the Green Belt, protect the character and appearance of the area, preserve the setting of the retained heritage assets, and protect the amenities of the surrounding area, in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies G2, D3, D4 and HC1 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies DMHB 1 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020).

No manufacturing, fabrication, assembly, testing of products, repair, servicing or other industrial processes associated with the use of the site shall take place outside the buildings hereby approved.
REASON

To safeguard the openness of the Green Belt, protect the character and appearance of the area, preserve the setting of the retained heritage assets, and protect the amenities of the surrounding area from noise and disturbance, in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (2026), Policies G2, D3, D4, D14 and HC1 of the London Plan (2021), and Policies DMHB 1, DMHB 11 and EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan.

The applicant is advised that bats and their roosts are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 (as amended) and the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 (as amended). The submitted bat surveys have confirmed the presence of bat roosts within buildings affected by the proposed development. A European Protected Species Mitigation Licence from Natural England will be required prior to any works that may affect bat roosts. The applicant should contact Natural England and a suitably qualified ecologist for further advice.

The applicant is advised that the approved access alterations within the public highway will require the prior approval of the Highway Authority and are likely to require the completion of a Section 278 Agreement under the Highways Act 1980. The applicant should contact the Council's Highway Authority at the earliest opportunity.

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to GRANT planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, in order to ensure that the applicant has been given every opportunity to submit an application which is likely to be considered favourably.
